posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
This week’s one-shot pits Wager Master against The Sentinels, XPW Argent Adept, Sky-Scraper, and Bunker.

It’s a randomized start, so you may not have gotten as lucky as I did, but this was the easiest One-Shot I’ve ever done.

First turn saw Wager Master put out Losing to the Odds and a couple Wagelings, so everyone took damage. Fortunately, The Sentinels started with 2 Unique Capabilities, so I played Hippocratic Oath to heal people to even numbers. Argent Adept and Sky-Scraper skipped their turns, Bunker played Adhesive Foam Grenade, and we won at the end of Wager Master’s second turn.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Match 1: He opened "Who Are You Fighting" and "What Do You Really Know", and I was pretty much toast.

Match 2: He opened "Not All He Seems", Wagelings, Wagelings, and Playing Dice With the Cosmos. I decided to go for the Not All He Seems win because I had Argent Adept ready to go with Bell / Bulwark / Inventive Prep, Sky-Scraper started with Neutralizing Resonator and Undetectable Relinking, and Bunker opened with Heavy Plating and Recharge Mode. So, we were able to tank all the Wageling damage, put his cards in the trash indiscriminately, and we thankfully dodged What Do You Really Know? both times. Unfortunately, Toxic Sludge came out and flipped Not All He Seems when I had Wager Master down to 2 cards in his deck. Fortunately, the top card remaining was Losing to the Odds and we won anyway.

Near Mint, can't feel bad about it because it's Wager Master on a random start, glad this didn't come up after my Mint streak of 26 earlier this year.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Whew, that one took a while.  "Who Are You Fighting?" was one of Wager Master's first cards, so I had to go fishing with Writhe's power for a Fling Into Darkness in order to win. That or hope Losing to the Odds came up and panned out just right, but it didn't.

It took waaaay longer than it should have.  You'd think that I'd come across a Fling, or a Team Communication or Unique Capabilities sooner rather than later....but the odds were not in my favor. Just Second Chances and Human Shields.

So. Many. Second. Chances.

Thankfully, Sky-Scraper had multiple Thorathian Monoliths and XPW AA had Vernal Sonatas to keep them coming back, so I could afford to wait it out....but it was a lot of waiting.

 

Eventually, a Fling happened, and Mainstay punched Wager Master into the shadowy Void.

 

Medico 10HP, Writhe 12HP, Idealist 10HP, Mainstay 9HP, XPW AA 18HP, Sky-Scraper 21HP, Bunker 23HP.

posts.name: carnilius
posts.cooked: Annoying slog of a Mint.  Got into a really long holding pattern with Mainstay with Chains and Human Shield and Tactics, Argent Adept Yelling at Medico to allow them to play a damage dealing card and double up on Mainstay's block, and also heal.  Sky Scraper put Compulsion Cannister on Mainstay to use Tactics and Block again, so we were able to ignore most damage, and heal a little every turn.  Finally ran out of cards for the Sentinels so we lost the shield.  Eventually killed Wager Master by beating him up.

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Near Mint.

First game started out with the New Deal, Losing to the Odds, Wagelings and Wagelings. It made it pretty much impossible to get evens without damage resistance, and Mainstay was the only source of that. I tried Thorathian Monolith to soak up damage, but I couldn't make it so Sky-Scraper ended up even hit points at the same time. Soon after, Playing Dice with the Cosmos came out, so the Sentinels couldn't take advantage of Argent Adept feeding Mainstay and tanking damage for the even condition. After two more Scum and Villainy cards and three Impossible Quandary cards, (one of which came up in Scum and Villainy) I was soon losing all my heroes. I tried to get Mainstay as the last hero standing where he could end the game with 2 hit points, but I couldn't pull it off.

Second game was the the nice easy win with Losing to the Odds. It took a few rounds, but it was much easier to pull off.

About the only other alternative I had in game 1 was trying to deck WagerMaster, but there was too much damage coming out and I spent turns focusing on getting evens somehow.

posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
Fffffffff

I lost the Mint after a huge amount of time because I was an idiot.

I was going for running out Wager Master's deck using Not All He Seems, combined with Writhe to take out his deck at double speed. I let Wager Master flip, got Not All He Seems back, and proceeded to wipe the rest of the cards. But I forgot that I had dropped Proportionist earlier, and then I played a Thorathian Monolith and accidentally pinged him for 1, which flipped it face-down. And then I got killed by An Unwise Wager when it flipped up while a deck was empty, which was just terrible luck.
